categories.name: It works
categories.notes: Build clean (0 errors, 0 warnings). / returns 200 through the '/' domain on the 'MCP Journal' page. It lists both posts as image cards with a kicker, title, summary and working links. Both posts render every block (hero, article) with no fallback text. The 3 provided Unsplash photos are imported into an 'MCP Journal' media folder and served through signed GetCropUrl URLs that load. Everything is published.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: Folders 8/8: blogFrontPage/blogPostPage in Pages; heroBlock, articleBlock and postFeedBlock are elements in Blocks. Block grid 4/7: one 'Blog Blocks' grid on both pages, but the set is only hero + article (heading + RTE) + post feed. There is no standalone image or text block, and each post is just a hero plus a single article block holding the whole body, which is the weak 'one rich text block' model. Structure 5/5: siteRoot is the only root type, siteRoot -> blogFrontPage -> blogPostPage, templates assigned, camelCase aliases, data type in Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid. Hygiene 2.5/5: no compositions and no duplicates, but posts have no metadata properties at all. There is no date anywhere. The listing card's title, summary and image are scraped from each post's first block (postFeedBlock.cshtml: post.Blocks?.FirstOrDefault()?.Content as HeroBlock), so cards break silently if an editor reorders blocks.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: Both templates use Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks"), and the scaffold blockgrid partials are unchanged. There are 3 adapters at Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml, each receiving BlockGridItem<T>, mapping to a plain class and calling Component.InvokeAsync, with no markup. The postFeedBlock adapter also queries children, which is acceptable. Three ViewComponents (in one file, ViewComponents/BlockViewComponents.cs) render Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml. Models are in Models/Blocks/, and the component views are plain. Program.cs and appsettings are untouched, there are no migrations, Children<T>/Parent<T>/Url()/GetCropUrl are used, and Tailwind is built. Minor: the full HTML shell (head/header/footer) is duplicated across blogFrontPage.cshtml and blogPostPage.cshtml with no shared layout.

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Content 4/6: both posts are on-topic and accurate ('MCP makes context useful, not just available.' and 'One protocol, many possibilities.'), with about 250 words over 5 paragraphs and 2 subheadings each. They are somewhat short and partly self-referential about the demo. Each post has only 2 blocks (hero + one article) and one relevant image. Presentation 4/4: a polished dark-hero Tailwind design with image credits, a 2-card listing with images, and a readable narrow article column with back links.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Channel/order 2.5/3: the Codex session exposed no Umbraco MCP tools. The model therefore spawned the project's own configured MCP server (npx @umbraco-cms/mcp-dev@18 from .mcp.json) over stdio from a temporary Python client (.mcp_blog.py, deleted at the end). All schema, media, content and domain writes went through that server's tools (create-element-type, create-and-publish-document, put-document-domains, etc.), so the channel is genuinely MCP. That is why the automated check sees 0 MCP calls. The model disclosed the workaround in its prompt-1 answer. Small deduction for one direct Management API shell call (a read-only GET /server/information connectivity probe) and for the writes being invisible to the harness. Order was right: model -> content -> stop/build/restart -> Razor. There was no memory access and no reads outside the project, apart from the allowed nuget XML docs. Honesty 2/2: the final report is accurate and makes no false claims.

summary: A clean, polished 'MCP Journal' blog built through the Umbraco MCP server (driven over stdio because the session exposed no MCP tools). It has a hero/article/post-feed block grid, two published MCP posts with the provided Unsplash photos, and a textbook adapter -> ViewComponent pipeline. The main weaknesses are the thin modeling: each post is just a hero plus one rich-text article block, there are no date or excerpt properties, and listing cards are scraped from each post's first block.
strengths: Everything works: clean build, '/' domain, both posts render, signed GetCropUrl images from the provided photos
Block pipeline exactly per AGENTS.md: GetBlockGridHtmlAsync, markup-free adapters, plain models in Models/Blocks, ViewComponents
Polished, coherent Tailwind design with image cards and credits
Adapted to missing MCP tools by driving the configured MCP server directly over stdio, disclosed it, and followed the model -> content -> restart -> Razor order

issues.text: Weak block model: each post is a hero plus one articleBlock (heading + RTE) holding the whole body. There is no standalone image or text block (Blog Blocks data type).

No post metadata properties (no date, excerpt or listing image) on blogPostPage. Cards are scraped from the post's first block in Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/postFeedBlock.cshtml (post.Blocks?.FirstOrDefault()?.Content as HeroBlock).
Posts are short (~250 words) and partly about the demo itself, with one image each.
HTML shell duplicated across Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml and Views/blogPostPage.cshtml; no shared layout.
One direct Management API shell call (read-only GET /umbraco/management/api/v1/server/information). MCP writes went through a hand-rolled stdio client, so they are invisible to the channel metrics.
